chapter.overview: This chapter details the architecture and operational mechanics of an AI tutor system, beginning with language model training protocols that emphasize dataset separation to prevent overstatement of performance. It explores the internal workings of decoder-only transformers, including tokenization, causal attention masks, and the distinction between attention weights and factual truth. The text further covers optimization techniques such as loss functions, backpropagation, and regularization methods like dropout and early stopping to mitigate overfitting. Post-training strategies are examined, specifically weight quantization for efficiency and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) for dynamic knowledge access without retraining. Finally, the chapter establishes a dual-evaluation framework that separates retrieval quality from answer generation, requiring tutors to explicitly identify conflicts in course passages rather than synthesizing unsupported conclusions.

The tutor uses a language model to generate explanations, but fluent wording does not guarantee factual accuracy. During training, the language model adjusts its parameters using examples from a training dataset. A separate validation dataset supports model selection and the choice of training settings. A held-out test dataset measures performance after those choices have been made. These datasets must be separated carefully: if passages from the same source appear in both training and testing, the measured performance can overstate the model's ability to handle unfamiliar material. Dataset size alone does not establish dataset quality.
